scenes.title: Ask a floor plan how many. See exactly where.
lines: Windows, doors, rooms and storeys, counted on the drawing itself.
Every counted item is marked where it is.
scenes.foot: Built at Junction 2026 for the Stoa, Verda and NVIDIA challenges
scenes.narration: This is Planproof. Ask a construction drawing how many windows, doors or bathrooms, and you get the number, with every counted item marked on the drawing.
It works on the sponsor's whole library: thousands of Finnish scans, Swiss plans and building models.
Here it found 18 windows. Every one is a mark on the scan, so you can check the count in seconds instead of trusting it.
It reads rooms too: kitchens, saunas, bathrooms and storeys, from the printed room names and a map of the plan. 3 floors, 3 boxes.
Even a zero comes with evidence. Here, the wet rooms it checked before saying there is no sauna.
What the local readers cannot prove, like showers, goes to NVIDIA's Nemotron. It reasons over the drawing and marks what it counted.

scenes.title: Local readers first, NVIDIA Nemotron for the rest
lines: 1. Room labels read with OCR on the scan.
2. Floor panels and the room map of a floor-plan detector.
3. Windows and doors read again at the drawing's own scale.
4. Anything still unproven goes to Nemotron on NVIDIA.
scenes.narration: Local readers go first, and only the unproven rest goes to NVIDIA. That keeps every answer fast, checkable and cheap.
